gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Synology DS1825neo+ ($1,189.99 on Amazon on 2026-11-13) is the DS1825+ with 4 GB of non-ECC RAM in place of 8 GB of ECC RAM. It has the same Ryzen V1500B with no integrated graphics, the same 2× 2.5GbE and the same PCIe slot, so it is $279.31 cheaper than the DS1825+ ($1,469.30) but no better for Plex. The QNAP TS-873A ($1,419.99) now costs $50 more than the UGREEN DXP8800 Plus ($1,369.99), and the TS-873A has no 10GbE built in.
standout_why: I compared against computingforgeeks.com/best-8-bay-nas (cited), wundertech.net/best-8-bay-nas-device-to-buy (cited), starryhope.com/nas/best-nas-for-plex (cited) and terabytewise.com/best-8-bay-nas. ComputingForGeeks names the DS1825neo+ only as a cheaper variant with no specs given. Terabytewise lists its $1,189.99 Amazon price but no specs. WunderTech and StarryHope don't mention it. One ChatGPT chat showed the neo+ at $1,189.99 and told the shopper to 'verify the exact neo+ model's features'. Nobody says it is the same box with 4 GB non-ECC RAM. ComputingForGeeks already gives price ranges, power draw and drive-inclusive totals, so the price spread itself is only partly new. Some ChatGPT chats put the TS-873A at $1,259–$1,288 and below the DXP8800 Plus; ComputingForGeeks' $1,400–$1,450 range already contradicts that.
decides: It confirms the DXP8800 Plus. At $1,369.99 it is the only model under $1,500 in ChatGPT's set (and in the rival lists) with Intel Quick Sync and built-in 10GbE. Each cheaper 8-bay loses for running Plex on the NAS: the neo+ and DS1825+ have no iGPU, the TS-832PX and UNAS Pro 8 are ARM, and the AS6508T is an older Atom. The TS-873A now costs more than the DXP8800 Plus and still needs a 10GbE card. For a shopper whose Plex server is a separate PC, the neo+ is the cheapest way into Synology DSM at 8 bays. It gives up ECC RAM and starts with half the memory.
